title: Computer Crime Proclamation 958/2016: court-warrant requirement for search and seizure
claim: The Ethiopian Computer Crime Proclamation No. 958/2016 requires the investigatory organ to obtain a court warrant before searching or accessing computer systems, networks or computer data for computer crime investigation.
evidence_summary: The Computer Crime Proclamation provides that where necessary for computer crime investigation, the investigatory organ may, upon getting a court warrant, search or access physically or virtually any computer system, network or computer data, and may seize computer systems or data during such searches.
source_excerpt: Search and Seizure 1/ Where it is necessary for computer crime investigation, the investigatory organ may, upon getting court warrant, search or access physically or virtually any computer system, network or computer data... 3/ In the execution of search... the investigatory organ may: a) seize any computer system or computer data; b) make and retain [copies].
interpretation: Normative evidence of judicial-authorization safeguards around state access to computer systems in Ethiopia. Establishes the legal procedural threshold; does not evidence investigative practice or compliance.
citation: Computer Crime Proclamation No. 958/2016, Search and Seizure provisions (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 83, 7 July 2016).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from primary legal text (search and seizure provisions).
keywords: computer crime, search and seizure, warrant, cybersecurity, Ethiopia

title: Computer Crime Proclamation 958/2016: admissibility and authentication of electronic evidence
claim: The Ethiopian Computer Crime Proclamation No. 958/2016 provides that electronic evidence produced in accordance with the Proclamation is admissible in court in relation to computer crimes, with the burden of proving authenticity on the person producing it.
evidence_summary: The Computer Crime Proclamation provides that electronic evidence produced in accordance with the Proclamation or obtained by appropriate foreign law enforcement bodies in accordance with Ethiopian law is admissible in court in relation to computer crimes, and places the burden of proving authenticity on the producer.
source_excerpt: electronic evidence: a) produced in accordance with this Proclamation; or b) obtained by appropriate foreign law enforcement bodies in accordance with Ethiopian Law shall be admissible in court of law in relation to computer crimes. 34. Authentication ... any person who produces evidences provided under Article 33 of this Proclamation in a court proceeding has the burden to prove its authenticity.
interpretation: Normative evidence of a statutory framework recognizing electronic evidence and digital authentication in Ethiopian criminal procedure. Establishes the legal basis; does not evidence judicial application.
citation: Computer Crime Proclamation No. 958/2016, admissibility and authentication provisions (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 83, 7 July 2016).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from primary legal text (electronic evidence provisions).
keywords: electronic evidence, admissibility, computer crime, Ethiopia
